where: Section 1, table row 'Short link or cable'
problem: The table treats a link and a cable the same. A cable or rope can only pull; a student may draw a cable reaction pushing on the body.
fix: Add: 'A cable or rope can only carry tension, so its reaction on the body always pulls along the cable. A two-force short link can push or pull, so its reaction may act either way along the link.'

problem: 'One force normal to the guide' is true only for a smooth collar free to rotate on the rod. A square slider held in a guide also prevents rotation.
fix: State the assumption: 'A smooth collar sliding on a rod gives one force normal to the rod. A square slider that cannot rotate in its guide gives a normal force and a moment; read the drawing to decide which one you have.'

problem: The count of three unknown reactions is treated as sufficient for stability. Three reactions that are all parallel, or all concurrent, still leave the body free to move.
fix: Add one sentence: 'Three reactions are necessary but not sufficient. If the three are all parallel or all pass through one point, the body can still move and the equations have no unique solution.'

problem: 'one arrow for a roller, two for a pin, three for a fixed support' compares arrows with components. A fixed support has two force arrows plus a moment, not three force arrows.
fix: 'one force arrow for a roller, two force arrows for a pin, two force arrows and one moment for a fixed support.'

where: Section 2, bullet list and the paragraph after it
problem: The negative-answer rule is stated in the bullet list and then stated twice more in the following paragraph, which makes the page slower to read than it needs to be.
fix: Keep the rule once, in the bullet list, and shorten the paragraph to: 'The assumed direction is free. A negative answer means the true direction is opposite your arrow. Write the units on every reaction: N for force, N·m for moment. A reaction moment appears only where rotation is prevented.'
